entries: Materials | Check and stage supplies | Verify labels, sizes and counts against the work order, then deliver supplies and tools to the assigned area.

Installation support | Supplies and grouting | Stage supplies in the specified sequence. The crew decides whether you assist with grouting.
Handling | Move stock as directed | Follow the assigned method for moving and placing supplies. Designated staff manage lifting, signals and the work area.
Cleanup | Tools and work area | Clean assigned areas and tools. The lead confirms cleaning products and repair plans.

Standards and quality boundaries | This page involves three types of requirements: first, technical and quality — ratios and cutting and tile setting and grouting and cleaning must be performed according to drawings and processes and current acceptance standards with material and work records kept; second, safety and occupational health — scaffolding and edges and openings and working at height and machinery and cutting and dust and chemical solutions and personal protection must meet building construction safety and occupational health requirements; third, environment and civilized construction — the disposal of waste slurry and wastewater and dust and noise and discarded materials must meet environmental protection and civilized construction requirements; all three are governed by the currently effective version and the requirements of the competent authority and the enterprise.

Records and collaboration | If safeguards fail, a hazard is unclear or a request exceeds the assignment, stop, step clear and tell the site lead. Keep original readings and times within your role. Designated staff decide on isolation, response and restart.

Role boundary | Helpers stage materials, pass tools and prepare or clean the work area as assigned. Brick and block masons build masonry, stonemasons cut and set stone, and tile setters lay and align tile. Ask who checks the work and who approves it.
Nearby roles | Decide whether you want to support several steps on a crew or train in a specific trade. Compare the first assignment, training and who checks the finished work.
Daily purpose | Keep the crew supplied and the work area ready. Check labels, quantities and dimensions against the work order, then report any mismatch.

How the trades differ | Brick and block masons build to layout drawings. Stonemasons cut and place stone. Tile setters check layout, joints and levels. Construction laborers cover a broader set of site tasks. Refractory repairers maintain heat-resistant linings.
What you check | Start with the work order, drawing revision and material labels. Confirm which tasks you may do and who checks any change.

Occupational profile | Masonry and tile helpers stage materials, pass tools and clean the work area. Depending on the assignment, they may check dimensions or help with mixing, cutting or grouting. Ask the employer what projects the crew handles, which tasks you would do and who checks the work.
Typical workflow | Helpers get materials and tools to the right place and keep the area ready. The crew’s trade determines which skilled work is performed and who checks it.
What you hand off | A staged batch, a clear work area and a short record of anything the crew still needs to verify.
What you hand off | Helpers hand over staged supplies and report discrepancies. Trade workers produce the finished masonry, stonework or tile installation.
Work records | Record the label, count or size and the person receiving the item. Preserve both entries when the work order and the label disagree.
Who checks adjacent work | Masons and tile setters produce the finished work for their trade. Ask the crew lead who checks the sample and who signs acceptance.

Helpers stage supplies, pass tools and clean assigned areas. Record discrepancies in labels, counts and sizes. Assist with mixing, cutting or grouting as directed. Designated staff decide on mix specifications, equipment operation and acceptance.
Approvals | If a drawing, material or structural detail changes, pause that step and give the original work order and change request to the designated project lead.

Confirm which tasks and tools you are authorized to use. Cutting equipment requires the site’s training, permission and safeguards. Scaffold work and lifting are assigned to people who meet applicable training, qualifications and authorization, under the required supervision.
Limits of a check | A label, measurement or sample check records what was verified for one step. Designated project staff decide on structural safety and final acceptance.
What helpers report | Write down what you measured, what differed and who should review it. Refer mix changes, scaffold acceptance and project release to designated staff.

Pre-onboarding checklist notes | The following six items are used to check off one by one before applying and onboarding, to avoid inferring actual duties and authorization from the job title or promotional language; the check results should be based on written recruitment information and the employment contract and job description and construction and safety system documents, and should be continuously confirmed after onboarding. This page only lists checklist points and does not constitute a hiring or safety conclusion.
Similar titles can lead to different assignments. Ask whether you would support a masonry, stone or tile crew and what tasks, tools, supervision and review the job involves.
01 Check the assignment | Ask who stages and cleans, who checks dimensions or changes a mix, who operates equipment and who reviews the work.

Work area check | O*NET asks separately about noise, contaminants, outdoor work and work at height. Cutting dust and cleaning products are examples tied to specific tasks. Actual exposure depends on the site and assignment.
02 Check safeguards | Ask if you would assist with cutting, lifting or work at height. Check what safeguards are required, who checks them and whom you should tell about a problem.

Job checklist | BLS Table 1.2 lists no formal educational credential and short-term on-the-job training as typical U.S. preparation. The O*NET apprenticeship directory gives examples of optional programs.
03 Education and training | Ask the employer about supervision, assigned work and any task-specific training, credentials or site authorization.

Before accepting the job, ask about the work area, materials, equipment, supervision and safeguards. Check whether you would move materials, cut stock or work outdoors and how you would hand off the work.

04 Check pay and hours | Ask about base pay, the pay period, shifts, overtime and work locations. Confirm the employment terms, training and benefits that apply at that location. Use national percentiles for market context.
Check the handoff | If a label and work order disagree, keep both entries and take the difference to the lead or materials contact.
05 Ask who signs off | Give the original label, size and count to the assigned reviewer. Ask who decides whether to proceed or approves a change or replacement.

Start a handoff with the work-order number, material label, size and count. Keep both entries when they disagree and give open items to the designated reviewer. Ask which form to use, where it is kept and who may edit it.
06 Check handoff records | Ask which labels, counts, dimensions and open discrepancies to record and which require the lead’s sign-off.

Typical support includes checking supplies, passing tools, cleaning and handing off discrepancies. Confirm the assignment for mixing, cutting or grouting. Trained, authorized workers operate the equipment.

Consider this trade if you want to lay out and build masonry.

Stonemasons (Stonemasons, 47-2022.00)
Tile setters lay and align tile and check the joints and level. Helpers prepare supplies and pass along mismatches or shortages.
Compare this path if you enjoy layout, joint spacing and leveling. A helper role offers more time staging and moving materials.
Typical output | Installed tile or stone with the specified joint spacing and level.
Tile and stone setters (Tile and Stone Setters, 47-2044.00)
Supports a broader range of site work. This helper role centers on masonry and tile crews.
Consider this direction if you want varied site tasks across trades.
Typical work | General site preparation, material handling and cleanup.
Construction laborers (Construction Laborers, 47-2061.00)
Repairs linings for industrial furnaces and kilns. Compare the specific equipment and setting before choosing a job.
Consider this trade if you want to work on heat-resistant industrial linings.
Typical output | Repaired refractory linings.
Refractory materials repairers, except brickmasons (Refractory Materials Repairers, Except Brickmasons, 49-9045.00)

subject.name: Masonry and Tile Helpers
subject.summary: Masonry and tile helpers stage and deliver supplies for brick, block, stone or tile crews. They check specifications and counts against the work order and clean assigned areas. Check site assignments, qualifications and controls before work involving saws, scaffolds or other restricted tasks.
